entry.title: Two Pointers (Same Direction)
entry.summary:
Overview
The Two Pointers (Same Direction) pattern uses two indices moving forward together through a data structure (usually an array or string).
Unlike opposite-direction pointers, both pointers only move left → right, but at different speeds or based on conditions. This pattern is extremely common in linear-time optimizations. Use this pattern when: You process elements in order
You want to compare or relate two positions
You need to skip, filter, or track a range
